instructions: Answer from the code as shipped (the answers do not depend on your fix). One option per question. Submit as {"Q1": "B", ...}.

questions.prompt: A bench rollout is at policy step 20 (the policy has been queried at steps 0 to 20). How many chunk predictions are averaged into the position command sent at step 20, and which of them has the largest weight?

options.A: 10 predictions; the one made at step 20 has the largest weight
options.B: 10 predictions; the one made at step 11 has the largest weight
options.C: 1 prediction: the chunk made at step 20 is executed open-loop, so nothing is averaged
options.D: 2 predictions, one per observation-history slot, weighted equally

questions.prompt: While aligning an episode, the operator's trigger goes from 0 to 1 at a leader sample stamped 2.437 s, and the policy grid has points at 2.4 s and 2.5 s (all times on the same clock). What gripper targets do the frames at 2.4 s and 2.5 s get?

options.B: 1 and 1 (the grid takes the next leader sample at or after each point)
options.D: 0 and 0 (the change shows up one frame later, at 2.6 s)

questions.prompt: Take the last aligned frame of an episode, with a fresh camera reading. It becomes a training sample with a 10-step action chunk. How many of those 10 chunk steps contribute to the training loss?

options.A: 1, for both the position term and the gripper term
options.B: 10: the steps past the end repeat the last action, which is the correct target for a robot that should stay put
options.C: 1 for the position term, 10 for the gripper term
options.D: 0: a frame whose chunk runs past the end of the episode is not turned into a sample

questions.prompt: When evaluate.py runs a trained checkpoint, where do the mean and standard deviation used to normalise the policy's inputs come from?

options.A: They are recomputed from data/demos each time evaluate.py starts
options.B: From all kept episodes, train and validation together, saved in the checkpoint
options.C: From the train-split episodes, but only the position columns: the other observation columns are passed through unnormalised
options.D: From the frames of the train-split episodes that have a usable camera reading, saved in the checkpoint and read back by the runner

questions.prompt: Episode 108 in data/demos produces no training or validation samples. Why?

options.A: Its camera stream has a gap longer than the 0.25 s limit
options.B: The span where all three streams have data is shorter than the 4.0 s minimum
options.C: Fewer than 80% of its camera frames detected the block
options.D: It lands in the validation split, which is only used for the loss curve

questions.prompt: On the bench, the block detector misses the block on some camera frames. On a policy step where the newest frame has no detection, what reaches the network's block_x / block_y inputs?

options.A: The position from the most recent frame that had a detection
options.B: A linear interpolation between the detections before and after the miss, as in training
options.C: NaN, which the normaliser turns into NaN outputs and the step is skipped
options.D: Nothing: the runner repeats the previous command without querying the network

questions.prompt: At the first policy step of a bench episode (right after reset), what fills the 'previous step' slot of the observation history, and is that consistent with how training samples were built?

options.A: Zeros; training also pads with zeros
options.B: The last observation of the previous episode, because the history is a deque that survives between episodes; training has no equivalent
options.C: A copy of the current observation; training also repeats frame 0 for the first frame
options.D: The normaliser's mean (zeros after normalisation); training repeats frame 0, so the two differ
